rows.title: Proposal Matrix builder: single decision surface aggregating internal + Codex + external proposals
rows.notes: Promoted to 'fixed' in Phase 2B-Revision P12. Build-WaggleProposalMatrix discovers iterations from epoch_evidence.json, reads internal Claude reviews (Phase 2A-2) + optional codex findings + optional latest valid external imports per (provider, role), populates linked_ledger_tags from text matches against the committed phase_fix_ledger.json, and populates linked_regressions from finding-id matches against state/regression_ledger.json. Outputs proposal_matrix.json + proposal_matrix.md (grouped by category). The synthesis paste-block (P9) inlines this as the primary decision surface.

rows.title: Regression Ledger with severity scoring (0-100), trajectory, status state machine
rows.notes: Promoted to 'fixed' in Phase 2B-Revision P12. RegressionLedger.ps1 exposes Get/Save (atomic .tmp + rename) / Add (auto REG-<UTC-date>-<NNN> id) / Update (legal-transition enforcement) / Get-Score (rubric: hardening_gate_failure=40, ci_failure=30, previously_passing_test_now_failing=25, runtime_crash=20, lock_state_signal=15, security_redaction=15, no_work_stall=10, source_supplement_sparse=10, doc_report_mismatch=5, cap 100) / Format-Excerpt (markdown for synthesis) / Write-Markdown (rendered file). Auto-update hook on hardening_gate_failure dedups by signature and is non-fatal.

rows.title: Dynamic epoch controller with verification gate, repair-attempt limits, severity-driven iteration ceiling
rows.notes: Promoted to 'fixed' in Phase 2B-Revision P12. EpochCycleTrigger now supports min=2 / target=3 / max=6 (hard ceiling), 8 decision states (continue / continue_for_repair / continue_for_verification / continue_for_auto_repair / trigger / strategic_external_review / halt / pause / needs_manual_action), repair caps medium=2/high=2/critical=1, same-issue resurrection escalation, same-test-failed-twice escalation, severity-cap (>=80 -> remaining=current+1, >=60 -> current+2), full audit record + Save-WaggleEpochControllerDecision, and a verification-iteration prefix builder. Test-EpochCycleTrigger covers ~58 cases across all branches.

rows.title: Auto-repair classifier + constrained repair prompt builder
rows.notes: Promoted to 'fixed' in Phase 2B-Revision P12. FindingClassifier returns one of {TRIVIAL_AUTO_FIX, LOCAL_REPAIR, EXTERNAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED, NEEDS_MANUAL_ACTION} via a fixability heuristic (file count, file:line presence, evidence-text patterns, unsafe/strategic keywords, force-external categories) + resurrection check against the regression ledger. Build-WaggleAutoRepairPrompt produces a tightly-constrained repair prompt with all 11 hard rules + an explicit SCOPE LIMIT clause + a repair_escalated.txt instruction for overflow. Test-FindingClassifier covers all four classes plus the heuristic + resurrection paths.

rows.title: Internal Claude review schema enhancement: reviewer_self_id + suggested_next_actions[]
rows.notes: Promoted to 'fixed' in Phase 2B-Revision P12. Both new fields are OPTIONAL on the Phase 2A-2 internal review schema; old reviews still validate. The validator enforces required sub-fields when reviewer_self_id is present, requires runtime='claude_code' for internal reviews, and validates estimated_effort enum on each suggested_next_action. The three internal review prompt templates request both blocks under a 'Phase 2B-Revision (SEC-009)' section. Test-ReviewSchema covers old/new/malformed shapes; Test-ReviewAdapter asserts the prompt files request both blocks.

rows.title: P5c regression-ledger hook silently downcasts critical/high review findings to severity=info
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI (gpt-5.5) in the Phase 2BR3 dual-engine simulation; Codex novel finding REL-001 (severity=high). Pre-fix bug: Add-WaggleRegressionFromInternalFinding accepted -Severity but never used it. score_categories carried only the category weight ('security_redaction'=15, 'lock_state_signal'=15) which translated to severity='info' (<20 band). Add-WaggleRegressionEntry's comment claimed 'Recompute severity from score if it's lower than the rubric implies' but the code always overwrote with the score-derived value. Therefore EVERY review finding routed through this hook with $Severity='critical' or 'high' landed in state/regression_ledger.json with severity='info', defeating the P5c hook's purpose. Fix: introduced _Rl-MaxSeverity helper using $Script:RLSeverityRank and applied it both inside the hook (input severity as floor) and inside Add-WaggleRegressionEntry (existing entry severity floors the score-derived value). Default-when-unset changed from 'medium' to 'info' so the floor logic gives correct semantics for low-score entries. New test cases in Test-RegressionLedger: 'critical input severity preserved', 'high input severity preserved', plus three _Rl-MaxSeverity unit checks. Test count: 49 -> 59.

rows.title: Save-WaggleRegressionLedger deletes old file before moving temp; crash window can lose ledger entirely
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 dual-engine simulation; Codex novel finding REL-002 (severity=medium). Pre-fix bug: Save-WaggleRegressionLedger ran Set-Content on $Path.tmp, then if the target existed: Remove-Item then Move-Item. A process crash, AV hold, disk error, or interrupted PowerShell session between Remove-Item and Move-Item left NO ledger at all (last good already deleted, replacement not yet in place). Fix: backup-and-replace sequence. Move existing $Path -> $Path.bak; Move-Item $tmp -> $Path; on failure, restore the .bak and re-throw; on success, drop the .bak. The previous ledger always survives until the new one is durably in place. New test cases: 'first save creates the ledger', 'second save replaces previous ledger durably', 'no .bak left behind after successful replace', 'no .tmp left behind after successful replace'.

rows.title: Redactor missing rule for URL-userinfo credentials and fine-grained GitHub PAT prefix
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 dual-engine simulation; Codex novel findings SEC-001 (URL userinfo) and SEC-002 (fine-grained GitHub PAT). Pre-fix bugs: (a) the Redactor had no rule for credentials embedded in URL userinfo (https://user:secret@host or https://x-access-token:secret@host) — git remotes and copied CLI output commonly carry these and the secret would leak into LLM packages. (b) The classic GITHUB_PAT pattern gh[psouri]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,} did NOT match the fine-grained PAT prefix github_pat_, and worse, Test-Redaction.ps1 had a comment '# 10. github_pat_ token redacted' immediately above a fixture using 'ghp_' — a test that lied about its coverage. Fix: added URL_USERINFO_CREDENTIAL rule with a host-port-safe pattern (the password segment disallows ':' so https://example.com:443/ is NOT matched), added GITHUB_FINE_GRAINED_PAT rule for the github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{82,} shape, corrected the misleading test comment, and added four new test cases (SEC-001a/b URL userinfo + host-port safety, SEC-002a/b fine-grained + classic regression). Test-Redactor count: 37 -> 45.

rows.title: Cockpit external-origin allowlist disagreed across header comment, footer text, and PROVIDER_URLS
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 dual-engine simulation; Codex novel finding architect-ARCH-003. Pre-fix the cockpit had four disagreeing sources of truth on which external origins are allowed: (a) HTML header comment listed gemini.google.com, grok.com, chatgpt.com, x.com/i/grok; (b) the visible footer omitted claude.ai; (c) the JS PROVIDER_URLS object had claude_web=https://claude.ai and did NOT have x.com/i/grok; (d) the ARCH-011 ledger note claimed claude.ai was in the whitelist. The cockpit is a manual trust-boundary tool — operators and reviewers could not tell which origin set was authoritative. Fix: PROVIDER_URLS is now declared the canonical source. Header comment + footer text both list gemini.google.com / grok.com / chatgpt.com / claude.ai (matching PROVIDER_URLS, with the unwired x.com/i/grok header entry removed). Test-CockpitData asserts every canonical host appears in the rendered HTML AND that the stale x.com/i/grok entry is gone. Test count: 36 -> 40.

rows.title: Source-supplement redaction omitted new URL-userinfo and fine-grained PAT rules
canonical_source_anchors: orchestrator/lib/Redactor.ps1 :: Phase 2B-R3 P10c (Codex post-fix SEC-001 fix)
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 post-fix dual-engine review (post-fix SEC-001 high). Pre-fix bug: P10 added GITHUB_FINE_GRAINED_PAT and URL_USERINFO_CREDENTIAL to DefaultRedactionRules, but NOT to SourceSupplementRuleNames. Phase 2A-4 deliberately uses a reduced source-supplement rule set; leaving the new value-shape rules out created a split-brain redactor where normal captured text was protected but LLM-bound source excerpts could still leak fine-grained PATs and URL-userinfo credentials. Codex's synthetic probe confirmed the leak. Fix: added both rules to SourceSupplementRuleNames. New Test-Redactor cases SS-SEC-001a/b verify the fix end-to-end through Invoke-WaggleSourceSupplementRedaction. Test-Redactor 45 -> 49.

rows.title: Severity floor was applied on insert but downcast on score_delta updates
canonical_source_anchors: orchestrator/lib/RegressionLedger.ps1 :: Phase 2B-R3 P10c (Codex post-fix REL-001 fix)
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 post-fix dual-engine review (post-fix REL-001 medium). The original REL-021 fix added a severity floor in Add-WaggleRegressionFromInternalFinding and Add-WaggleRegressionEntry — but Update-WaggleRegressionEntry's score_delta branch assigned severity = _Rl-SeverityFromScore unconditionally, downcasting any pre-existing high/critical severity back to info on the next update. Fix: apply _Rl-MaxSeverity to existing severity AND score-derived severity in the score_delta branch too. Now the floor is consistent across the entry lifecycle (insert + every later update). New Test-RegressionLedger cases verify: insert with critical preserved on no-op delta, on negative delta, and that positive delta still allows upward severity. Test-RegressionLedger 62 -> 66.

rows.title: Schema rejected runtime score_categories field but contract documented it as preserved
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 post-fix dual-engine review (post-fix architect ARCH-001 medium, persists). The schema had additionalProperties=false and did not declare score_categories; the runtime writer used score_categories on every entry (Get-WaggleRegressionScore consumes it); the ARCH-009 fix added a doc note explaining 'survives storage'. Codex flagged that this kept a schema-vs-runtime split-brain alive even after the original ARCH-009 fix. Fix: added score_categories as an optional persisted property in the schema (matching the runtime behavior) with a description that explicitly documents it as the runtime-rubric input field for Get-WaggleRegressionScore. Schema validation now matches what RegressionLedger.ps1 actually writes. The ledger_contract.md note about it remains accurate.

rows.title: ledger_contract.md dedup section described non-existent updated_at_utc and seen_count fields
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 post-fix dual-engine review (post-fix architect ARCH-002 medium new_in_fix). Pre-fix the contract claimed re-fired hooks 'bump updated_at_utc and increment seen_count' — neither field exists in the schema or runtime writer. The actual behavior (per Add-WaggleRegressionFromHardeningGateFailure / Add-WaggleRegressionFromInternalFinding / Add-WaggleRegressionsFromReviewObject) is to call Update-WaggleRegressionEntry with a history_event(event=detected, notes=repeat <kind>: <id>), and the entry's history[] array grows by one element per re-fire. Fix: rewrote the Dedup contract paragraph to describe the actual Get-WaggleIssueSignature signature shape (with deliberately empty IterationIdIntroduced for cross-iteration stability) and the history_event-append behavior (timestamp lives in history[].at_utc, count is history[].length). Doc-only fix; no test added (covered by ledger_contract.md presence + ARCH-009 schema-grounded gate).

rows.title: ledger_contract.md described stale runtime-ledger schema and helper names
rows.notes: Found by Codex CLI in the Phase 2BR3 dual-engine simulation; Codex novel finding architect-ARCH-001 (severity=medium). Pre-fix docs/design/ledger_contract.md (the deliverable that R3's Test-LedgerContract was supposed to enforce) was MATERIALLY incorrect: it claimed runtime helpers Ensure-WaggleRegressionLedger and Set-WaggleRegressionState (neither exist; actual writers are Get-WaggleRegressionLedger / Save / Add / Update), and listed an entry-field set (entry_id, finding_id, signature, state, dedup_key) that did not match the actual schema (id, detected_in_iteration, category, first_symptom, severity, score, status, history, score_categories). The R3 gate enforced only proose-fragment phrases, not the materially-correct contract — meaning a future contributor following the 'authoritative document' would code against a non-existent API. Fix: rewrote the Schema and Authoritative writer rows of the TL;DR table to match schemas/regression_ledger.schema.json + orchestrator/lib/RegressionLedger.ps1 verbatim; rewrote the State-machine bullet to enumerate actual states from $Script:RLStatuses; replaced 'Ensure-WaggleRegressionLedger' with 'Get-WaggleRegressionLedger (creates empty if absent)' throughout; added strict Test-LedgerContract assertions for required helper names + canonical entry fields + a denylist of stale names that must NOT reappear. Test-LedgerContract count: 17 -> 27.

rows.title: Redactor SHA-context allowlist does not survive JSON-encoded diff_text strings
rows.notes:
P9 architect review of PR #94 found that GIT_LOG_LINE only matched at line-start (?im)^commit\s+<sha>, which never fires inside a JSON-encoded string where '
' is the literal two-char escape. Phase 2BR2 P2 added a sibling rule GIT_LOG_LINE_JSON_ESC matching '
' or '
' preceding 'commit <hex40>'. New regression tests in Test-Redactor.ps1 (ARCH-001a..d) cover: 40-hex SHA inside JSON-escaped diff_text preserved; PR commit SHA in git_metadata.json preserved; PR commit SHA inside JSON-escaped diff_text preserved; SHA preserved AND inline secret redacted in same blob. Test-Redactor count: 27 -> 37.

rows.title: Redactor AWS_SECRET_KEY pattern eats long PowerShell identifiers
rows.notes: P9 architect review of PR #94 found the prior pattern (?<![A-Za-z0-9/+=])[A-Za-z0-9/+=]{40}(?![A-Za-z0-9/+=]) accepted any 40-char run from the AWS class, including pure-alpha PowerShell function names like 'Add-WaggleRegressionFromHardeningGateFailure'. Phase 2BR2 P2 tightened the pattern with two zero-width lookaheads requiring at least one digit AND at least one of '/+=' inside the 40-char window. Real AWS secret-access-key shapes still match. Bonus side effect: pure-hex 40-runs (commit SHAs) no longer trip the AWS rule even outside SHA-context positions, so the GitShaContext rules become defence-in-depth rather than load-bearing. New regression tests in Test-Redactor.ps1 (ARCH-002a..c) cover: 40+ alpha PS identifier preserved; real AWS-shape redacted in env context; pure-hex 40-run not eaten.

rows.title: review_cockpit.html lives at repo root with no containing layer

Phase 2BR2 P3 git-mv'd review_cockpit.html under orchestrator/cockpit/, added orchestrator/cockpit/README.md describing the cockpit_data.json contract + 5s polling + origin allowlist, and updated Open-WaggleCockpit.ps1 to resolve the new path with a backward-compat fallback to the legacy repo-root location for in-flight worktrees. Test-CockpitData adds three new assertions: cockpit file exists at orchestrator/cockpit/, legacy repo-root cockpit removed, README exists. Test-CockpitData count: 30 -> 32.

rows.title: Dual-ledger contract (phase_fix_ledger vs regression_ledger) is implicit
rows.notes: P9 architect review of PR #94 noted phase_fix_ledger.json (committed) and state/regression_ledger.json (gitignored runtime) had overlapping conceptual surface but no documented contract. Phase 2BR2 P4 added docs/design/ledger_contract.md stating: phase_fix_ledger = committed historical record; regression_ledger = live runtime state machine; cross-link rules used by Build-WaggleProposalMatrix; what survives a clean clone; when to write where. Phase 2BR3 P1 (PM-CL-002 from R2 architect review) converted the markdown-only contract into an enforced hardening gate at orchestrator/Test-LedgerContract.ps1: asserts phase_fix_ledger.json + .md + ledger_contract.md committed; runtime ledger NOT committed outside an explicit allowlist; contract doc references both ledgers; Build-WaggleProposalMatrix tolerates missing state/regression_ledger.json on a clean clone. 16 assertions; gate count 29 -> 30.

rows.title: Cockpit fetch URL not updated after orchestrator/cockpit/ relocation
rows.notes: Phase 2BR2 PR #97 ARCH-005 git-mv'd review_cockpit.html from repo root to orchestrator/cockpit/ but the JS fetch URL was a literal 'state/cockpit_data.json' which is relative-to-the-HTML-location. From the new location that resolves to orchestrator/cockpit/state/cockpit_data.json which does not exist. Test-CockpitData (32/32) still PASSED because it asserted only the LITERAL string match, not URL resolution from the cockpit's actual location. Operator hit 'Could not load state/cockpit_data.json: Failed to fetch' after opening file:///C:/Python/project2-master/orchestrator/cockpit/review_cockpit.html in browser. Fix: introduce COCKPIT_DATA_URL constant '../../state/cockpit_data.json'; user-visible strings still refer to the canonical 'state/cockpit_data.json' filename. New Test-CockpitData assertion resolves the relative URL from the cockpit's directory and asserts it lands on repo-root state/cockpit_data.json. Test count: 32 -> 34. Caveat: even with the path fix, modern Chrome/Edge block file:// fetches to file:// resources by default; if 'Failed to fetch' persists after the fix, the operator must either pass --allow-file-access-from-files to the browser or serve via a local static HTTP server.

rows.title: Invoke-WaggleReview top-level CLI dereferences $r.role on -DryRun pscustomobject which lacks role
rows.notes: Found in Phase 2B-R1 P9 while priming the architect self-review with a -DryRun shape check. The DryRun branch returned a pscustomobject WITHOUT 'role' or 'target_iteration_id'; the top-level CLI wrapper at the bottom of the script does Write-Host (...$r.role, $r.target_iteration_id, ...) under StrictMode in BOTH success and failure paths, which throws PropertyNotFoundStrict. Phase 2B-R1 (P10) routed this EXTERNAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED / fixability_ambiguous because the proposed-fix string offered multiple shapes; recorded as backlog. Phase 2B-R2 P5 reproduced via direct dry-run invocation (Test-ReviewRunner) and confirmed the cleanest fix is to make the DryRun return object carry the same identity fields ('role', 'target_iteration_id', 'status') as the non-DryRun branch. New assertions in Test-ReviewRunner.ps1 ('dry-run: returns role property', 'dry-run: returns target_iteration_id property', 'dry-run: returns status property') lock this in. Test count: 69 -> 72.
